title: Great Leadership Is Both a Generous and a Selfish Act
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Admired Leadership argues that leadership at its best is both generous and selfish. The post first lists the generous side: coaching, challenging, including others in decisions and sacrificing time so others can excel. It then turns to the self-serving side, in which every act of teaching or mentoring also sharpens the leader's own thinking. The claim is that leaders who pursue their own growth most deliberately end up helping others best. A Ram Dass quotation closes the piece, and even servant leaders are said to take satisfaction from serving.
points: Leadership in its best form is generous: coaching, challenging, including and sacrificing for others.
Teaching and mentoring also improve the leader by forcing clarity about their own choices.
Pursuing personal growth deliberately makes a leader better at helping others succeed.
Even servant leaders derive self-satisfaction from service, so generosity and self-interest are not opposed.
quotes: They coach, guide, direct, and facilitate others as a means of making them more skillful, productive, and satisfied. They challenge others with long-term goals and visions that are larger than themselves.
But every time a leader teaches, coaches or mentors others to a better outcome, they also make themselves better. By working to improve others, they invariably improve themselves.
By explaining and showing others how to make the most of situations, they absorb their own lessons, creating a clarity of thinking and doing that informs their own choices.
Ironically, the more selfish a leader is to achieve personal growth and development, the better they are at helping others succeed. They learn about themselves with every choice they make for others.
Even servant leaders appreciate the fact that they derive great self-satisfaction from service. The more they serve others, the more they learn how to serve themselves.
I help people as a way to work on myself, and I work on myself to help people.” Working on themselves by helping others is what great leaders do.
